correctness.rationale: Coordinatewise multiplication makes \(\operatorname{ann}(x)\) depend only on the complement of \(\operatorname{supp}(x)\), and Badawi adjacency is exactly incomparability of supports. A total-dominating two-set must itself be an edge. If its supports intersect, the intersection-support vertex is comparable with both and undominated; if their union is proper, the union-support vertex is undominated. Thus the supports are complementary. Conversely, any proper nonempty support must be incomparable with at least one side of a complementary bipartition, proving domination. Counting unordered support bipartitions and the vertices in each support class gives the formula. The finite checker is corroborative only.

final_claim: For a finite reduced nonfield ring \(R\cong\prod_{i=1}^r\mathbb F_{q_i}\), the minimum total and paired dominating sets of the annihilator graph are exactly the vertex pairs with complementary coordinate supports; both parameters equal two and the exact number of minimum sets is \((2^{r-1}-1)\prod_i(q_i-1)\).
limitations: Finite reduced commutative rings only; nilpotents are excluded.
Only minimum total/paired sets are classified, not all higher-cardinality dominating sets.
